learning_outcomes.text: Proper implementation of specific fundamental knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry, in the field of electrical engineering
Use of fundamental concepts of computer science and information technology
Use of fundamental knowledge of electrotechnics
Design of electrical systems and their components
Acquire mathematical skills in solving problems of electric and electromagnetic field, the use of signals in time and frequency.

Know how to use and apply mathematical formulas, within the studied chapters such as: symbolic analysis, partial differential equations, time and frequency analysis required for electrical engineering applications in the following disciplines to be performed during the 4 years of study.

syllabus_topics: Scalar fields. Vector fields.
Analysis of electrical signals over time. Applications with the 20 SIM simulation program.
Use of functions for modeling complex systems.
Methods of modifying equations. Applications with the 20 SIM simulation program.
Power and energy variables. Input sizes
Analysis of the system of equations for an electrical circuit
Modeling of direct current electrical circuits in the 20 Sim simulation program.
Making connection graphs for simple electrical circuits.
Procedures for constructing connection graphs for electrical circuits.
Checking the current and voltage characteristics for direct current electrical circuits using classical methods and simulation in 20 SIM.

Verification of Kirchhoff's Theorem I for direct current circuits by applying the simulation method in 20 SIM. Comparison of the results obtained in 20 SIM with the results obtained by the classical method.

Verification of Kirchhoff's Theorem II for direct current circuits by applying the simulation method in 20 SIM. Comparison of the results obtained in 20 SIM with the results obtained by the classical method.

Comparison of the results of some electrical circuits that are in direct current solved using the theorem of cyclic currents with simulation results using the connection graphs and the simulation program 20 SIM
Comparison of the results of some direct current electrical circuits solved using the potential theorem at nodes with simulation results using the connection graphs and the 20 SIM simulation program

assessment_rules: The final grade N is calculated as 70% from the exam (Ex) and 30% from the seminar (S). Conditions for obtaining credits are N ">= 5", S ">= 5", L ">= 5", and P ">= 5". Minimum performance standard requires adequate use of basic knowledge of mathematics, physics, and chemistry in developing a professional project of low complexity.
